statement: For three general circles the ordinary complex circle problem has degree 8. The four quadratic branches give at most eight geometric circles; Stoll’s regular eight-real cases attain this upper bound, so the generic complex degree is eight. Opposite signed-radius descriptions are identified.

answer.qualification: Explicit consequence of Stoll’s quadratic branch calculation and a regular eight-real case. Ordinary geometric circles, not oriented signed-radius duplicates or exceptional point/line circles.

source.location: Equations (31)–(34), original p. 625; unnumbered table on p. 626, cases 1, 6 and 10.

scope: Three general labelled complex circles as inputs; distinct ordinary geometric solution circles tangent to all three, modulo the signed-radius duplication. Exclude point circles, limiting lines and exceptional quadratic-branch charts.
